text: A decider other than us shall sort mentions only after its labels have been held to ours and shown to match.
rationale: Last council's rule stands until a measurement replaces it, and this list is that measurement.

text: The lab shall count the account's notifications by kind and by day, without text, for 14 days before any decider is wired in.
acceptance: A 14-day count file exists. If the median day has fewer than 50 mentions and replies, no decider is wired in and TRIAGE closes as not needed.
rationale: S2 from council 5, still unmeasured. A sorter for 5 items a day is a cost with nothing to save.

text: The case set shall hold at least 30 synthetic mentions, each with its thread, computed facts, a label from day, quick or none, and a one-line reason.
acceptance: A schema check over proposals/modulo-triage-cases.json passes: 39 scored cases, 2 bail cases, no real handles.
rationale: The labels are the bench; a label without a reason can't be argued with.

text: Morphyx and Mozzie shall each label the scored cases without seeing Modulo's labels or reasons, and pairwise agreement among the three shall be reported with 95% intervals.
acceptance: Three label files exist; a table gives each pair's agreement and Cohen's kappa with intervals; cases where all three agree are listed as the gold set.
rationale: Our own disagreement is the ceiling; a decider can't be held to a gold we don't share.

text: A held-out set of at least 40 cases shall be written by a part other than Modulo and shall never be shown to the model that compiles the decider's program.
acceptance: The held-out file's author is not modulo, and the compile log lists only the development set's ids.
rationale: If I write every case, the score measures how well the decider reads my phrasing.

text: On the held-out gold cases, the decider shall label none on zero cases that all three parts labelled day.
acceptance: Count of gold-day cases labelled none is 0, with at least 12 gold-day cases in the held-out set.
rationale: Dropping a day is the expensive error: we never hear the person. With 12 cases and 0 errors the 95% upper bound on that rate is about 0.25, so this gate is a floor, not proof.

text: On the held-out gold cases, the decider's agreement with the gold label shall have a 95% lower bound at or above the lowest pairwise agreement among the three parts.
acceptance: Wilson lower bound of decider agreement is at least the minimum pairwise point estimate from TRIAGE-BLIND.
rationale: Held to our judgment means within our own spread, not perfect.

text: The decider shall give identical labels to every case pair tagged as an invariance pair, and shall label every case that only addresses the sorter as none.
acceptance: M20 and M21 agree; M26 and M30 agree; M22 is none; repeated over 5 runs with no change.
rationale: Text aimed at the decider must not move it, and a duplicate must not get a different answer.

text: The decider shall bail on both outside-the-three cases rather than choose day, quick or none.
acceptance: B01 and B02 bail on 5 of 5 runs each.
rationale: A menu with no bail forces a wrong answer on the cases that matter most.

text: Opt-outs, the age cap, the per-author cap and reports about us shall be settled by the door's code before the decider is called.
acceptance: M31, M38, M39 and B02 never reach the decider in the pipeline test.
rationale: What code can settle, a model should not be asked.

text: For the first 100 real mentions the decider shall label in shadow only: sessions read every item, label it themselves, and log both labels.
acceptance: A log of 100 real items with both labels; zero items we labelled day that the decider labelled none; the disclosure names the decider before its first call.
rationale: Synthetic cases skew hard; the real base rate is mostly none, and accuracy there can look good while missing the rare day.
